newsitem.title: PERU: Japan's Aoki knew of Peru raid plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Aoki knew of Peru raid plan - paper.

text.p: Japan's ambassador in Peru knew in advance of a plan to storm his home in a bid to rescue 72 hostages and urged peace brokers to speed up negotiations to avoid a bloody end to the siege, a Lima newspaper reported Friday.

According to the report in respected daily El Comercio, Morihisa Aoki had learned at the beginning of April from captive army and police generals of a plan to attack the residence while the rebels played soccer in a downstairs reception room.

Once he knew of the plan, Aoki wrote a letter to Tokyo's point man in the crisis, Terusuke Terada, to inform him and urge him to accelerate talks between the government and the rebels in search of a peaceful end to the crisis.
The report, which cited unnamed diplomatic sources, said Aoki told Terada in the letter that the assault was scheduled for the end of the first week of April.
Crack Peruvian troops stormed Aoki's home Tuesday, bursting in through tunnels to surprise the rebels as they played soccer.
The raid secured the rescue of all but one of the 72 hostages. Two army officers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas were killed in the attack.
